attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his view.

semantics.note: "Definitely think" is a firm factual assertion that generative AI was used. The quality and volume remark is his reason, not a separate claim to score. "Here" could mean Dudesy broadly or the Carlin special, but the drafter's choice is reasonable.

contract.note: The broad reading (script, voice or imagery) is the ordinary meaning of "used here". The result depends on that reading: human authorship of the script alone would decide the narrow reading differently. The contract correctly separates script work from voice and image work.

evidence.note: Smithsonian says the spokesperson described the special as human-written and then voiced by an AI voice generator. That is secondhand, and other reports of the same disclosure conflict with it, so the support is weak.
The spokesperson says Kultgen wrote the whole special. This rules out AI-written jokes but says nothing either way about the voice.
Says the spokesperson did not comment on whether the voice was AI. This undercuts Smithsonian's version of what she said.
The case settled before discovery, so it is unclear which parts were AI-generated. This confirms the evidence gap.

reviews.rationale: The only support is Smithsonian's secondhand account that the voice was AI-generated, and MovieMaker and the Guardian contradict or qualify it. The script was reportedly human-written. No production records or firm creator disclosure establish or rule out generative AI in the voice or imagery, so the packet does not settle the claim.

semantics.note: Keeps all three figures and the nine-month window. "AI-themed" is a harmless descriptor.

contract.note: Reading these as cumulative YouTube views at the time of writing, with ordinary tolerance for "around", is a fair plain reading.

reviews.rationale: No evidence items were recovered. No contemporaneous view counts exist in the packet for the first episode, the nine-month episode cohort, or the Carlin upload, so the figures cannot be verified or contradicted.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: "Will have forgotten" is firm, and the "unless the estate sues" exception is kept. The quality judgments and his stated hope are rightly left unscored.

contract.note: Treating a lawsuit within the two-week window as triggering the exception, rather than as failure, is fair to his words.

evidence.note: The complaint naming the estate's executor was filed on January 25, 2024, inside the window. This defeats the no-lawsuit condition but is not evidence about whether people forgot the special.

reviews.rationale: The estate sued on January 25, 2024, before the January 30 deadline. That triggers the speaker's explicit exception, so the forecast's condition was never met. Under the contract's early-resolution rule the prediction is inapplicable and cannot be scored.
